title: Auditing Questionable Research Practices and Drafting an OSF Preregistration
description: Detect p-hacking and HARKing in a simulated research trajectory, then draft a formal Open Science Framework preregistration protocol.
problemStatement:
Examine this research narrative: *'Dr. Miller tests whether lighting scents (lavender vs. citrus vs. unscented) alter creative problem-solving. At N = 20, p = 0.14. She collects 10 more subjects; p = 0.08. She excludes 3 participants who reported allergies; p = 0.054. She transforms the data using a log-scale and controls for participant caffeine intake; p = 0.041! She discards the citrus condition entirely and writes the journal article claiming lavender uniquely enhances problem-solving based on evolutionary scent theory.'*

### Your Mission:
1. **Identify Four Questionable Research Practices (QRPs)**: Flag four specific QRPs committed by Dr. Miller in this scenario (e.g., data peeking, post-hoc outlier exclusion, p-hacking via covariates, HARKing/selective reporting).
2. **Calculate the False-Positive Risk**: Explain how these repeated 'researcher degrees of freedom' artificially inflate the actual false-positive (Type I) error rate far above the nominal α = 0.05 level.
3. **Draft an OSF Preregistration Section**: Write the 'Planned Sample Size and Exclusion Rules' and 'Statistical Analysis Plan' sections of an Open Science Framework (OSF) preregistration that would eliminate every one of Dr. Miller's methodological indiscretions.
hints: Hint 1: Check how Dr. Miller peeked at data and stopped only when p crossed 0.05 (optional stopping).
Hint 2: In a preregistration, exclusion rules (e.g., 'participants with allergies will be excluded prior to testing') must be locked in advance.
